correctness.rationale: The universal competitor with singleton sites 1,...,n-2, one centroid on {n-1,n}, and a geometric tail centroid on n+1,... has distortion U_n=2^(3-n)/3: pair cost 2^(1-n)/3 and tail conditional variance 2 times mass 2^-n. If an optimal interval Voronoi cell merged r,r+1 with r≤n-3, its two-atom distortion is at least d_r=w_r w_(r+1)/(w_r+w_(r+1)). For distinct early dyadic-permuted masses d_r≥2^(2-k)/3>U_n; at the k-1 to k boundary d_r≥2^(1-k)/3≥U_n; in the geometric tail d_r=2^-r/3≥U_n. Additional positive distortion outside any pair makes total V_n>d_r, contradiction. Ordered Voronoi intervals and centroid property then force the first n-3 centers to be singleton atoms. Independently evaluated 25,394 exact rational pair inequalities over k=2..7 permutations; arbitrary-k theorem rests on symbolic inequalities.

originality.rationale: Gomez et al. (2023) Theorem 1.3 assumes the exact singleton property and Conjecture 1.5 explicitly asks to prove it for all finite initial dyadic permutations, verifying only two worked distributions (pp.3-5). Their conditional tail solution cannot imply the premise. The uniform adjacent-pair lower bound supplies an unconditional missing argument for every permitted permutation. Cabasag et al. earlier work on the ordinary geometric law is a special parameter choice.
